description: One address in front of a pool of servers that picks a server for each request and forwards it.
Picks the servers of the pool in order and wraps around, spreading requests evenly across similar servers.
A periodic probe (or a watch on real traffic) that marks a server down after failures and up after successes.
A component whose failure stops the whole system, such as a lone load balancer.
Keeping the system up through failures by running redundant copies of every component on the request path.
The balancer sends a user to the same server every time, usually with a cookie; that server's failure still loses its in-memory state.
